answer: Neighborhood Cutoff: each agent's local mirror of the transaction graph weights counterparties by path redundancy. An agent whose links are overwhelmingly single-path gets its traffic deprioritized as a hollow signal, since real participation leaves overlapping routes. Enforcement: edge weight scales with distinct two-hop paths, so one agent must sustain many independent, genuinely active counterparties per identity. Cost: roughly N extra maintained relationships and their message overhead per sybil, rising with the cutoff threshold.
